To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Web is a useful survey technology for gathering data from managers, but that it is best to combine Web and fax surveys in order to increase response rates.

(1) the Web technology yielded a lower response rate than other technologies, (2) computer-based technologies (i.e., Web, disk) yielded higher item completion than mail, and (3) computer-based technologies may yield a sample of respondents that exhibit forecasting characteristics associated with best practices.
(1) the Web is not a panacea, but (2) it can be an effective survey technology for operations management research when combined with fax and mail.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the Web for data collection in the context of a large-scale establishment-level survey.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Web-based surveys can be effective for some populations, but are not a panacea for all survey populations.
Web surveys are an effective means of collecting data from managers, but only if the manager has access to e-mail.
the use of the Web technology for surveys of managers in large and medium-sized manufacturing and service organizations should be avoided.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Web is a viable technology for gathering data in operations management, but it is not the panacea it is sometimes made out to be.
Web surveys are still not a viable alternative to traditional surveys.
the Web technology is still not ready for prime-time in the area of establishment-level surveys.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Internet has not yet reached a level of maturity where it is a viable survey technology for gathering establishment-level survey data.
the Web survey technology is not yet a practical alternative to the mail survey, especially for gathering establishment-level survey data.
Web technology is not a panacea for all research problems and that the Web is not the only technology that can be used to gather data from large numbers of firms.
